subject: Social Studies
name: JHS 1 Social Studies
description: The JHS 1 Social Studies curriculum introduces learners to environmental issues, mapping skills, family life, self-identity, citizenship, and socio-economic development. It emphasizes understanding the world, responsible citizenship, and national identity

strands.title: ENVIRONMENT
strands.description: Understanding environmental issues and mapping skills

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate skills in dealing with environmental challenges

indicators.description: Examine ways of dealing with sanitation challenges in the environment

exemplars.description: Explain Environment and Sanitation
Discuss the types of environment (physical and social)
Identify some environmental problems, including poor sanitation
Examine cultural practices and their related problems for sanitation in the community
Discuss the effects of poor sanitation practices
Identify different ways of managing sanitation problems
Embark on a project with the aim of managing sanitation problems in the community

contentStandards.description: Examine the sources of energy and demonstrate the skills of conserving energy in Ghana

exemplars.description: Explain energy
Describe the sources of energy in Ghana, including fuel wood, hydro, solar and thermal
Categorise sources of energy into renewable and non-renewable

indicators.description: Examine the benefits of using renewable and non-renewable energy

exemplars.description: Examine the benefits of using renewable energy
Examine the benefits of using non-renewable energy sources
Design posters to show how different sources of energy are used
Discuss how sun or wind can be used to heat or perform work
Come out with ways of using energy
Discuss why Ghana sometimes imports energy

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate a range of mapping skills

indicators.description: Demonstrate skills involved in mapping and locating places in the environment

exemplars.description: Explain 'maps' and 'scale'
Identify types of maps, including street maps, maps showing landscape features and national maps using an atlas
Explore the importance of maps to different people
Identify components of maps, including north arrow, scale, map key allowing representation of physical and human features
Sketch a map of the school compound, marking the main features
Locate some important landmarks in the community using maps

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of the world around us

indicators.description: Examine major physical features of the earth

exemplars.description: Identify some major features of the earth such as mountain ranges, rivers, oceans, hot deserts and tropical rainforest
Find the locations of major physical features using maps
Discuss human activities that affect features and ways of protecting them
Discuss the effects of plastic pollution on water bodies

contentStandards.description: Assess the issue of natural disasters and their management

indicators.description: Examine natural disasters in the environment

exemplars.description: Explain natural disasters
Watch documentaries on some natural disasters
Mention examples of natural disasters
Identify natural disasters in Ghana
Suggest ways to manage disasters
Discuss the role of institutions responsible for early detection and management of natural disasters in Ghana

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of adolescent behaviour and reproductive health issues

indicators.description: Examine issues on adolescent behaviour and reproductive health

exemplars.description: Explain the concepts: Adolescence and Reproductive Health
Discuss adolescent behaviours, including chastity that would support reproductive health
Discuss why healthy behaviour during adolescence is important
Invite a resource person to talk about how some adolescent behaviours can harm their reproductive health
Explain changes that adolescents go through
Discuss some challenges faced by adolescents

contentStandards.description: Exhibit knowledge of the importance of socialisation

indicators.description: Examine the place of socialisation in developing the individual

exemplars.description: Explain the meaning of socialisation
Explain the terms: Agencies and Agents
Identify the agencies and agents of socialisation
Discuss the roles of agencies and agents in the socialisation process
Role-play and embark on a socialising project
Find out the need for socialisation and the challenges associated with it

contentStandards.description: Analyse the population structure in Ghana and its related issues

indicators.description: Examine the components of population growth

exemplars.description: Explain the concept of population growth
Discuss how population in Ghana has changed in the recent past
Compare Ghana's population growth with that of some other countries
Discuss factors of population change: Birth rate, Death rate, Migration
Investigate the causes of high birth rates and high death rates in Ghana

contentStandards.description: Show understanding of self as a unique individual

exemplars.description: Explain the concepts "self" and "self-identity"
Identify attitudes that enhance self-worth
Identify one's strengths and weaknesses as unique individual
Examine the reasons for knowing oneself
Describe how an individual can develop their capabilities

contentStandards.description: Analyse the responsibilities of a citizen

indicators.description: Examine the value of citizenship in nation building

exemplars.description: Explain the concept of "citizenship"
Discuss the various ways of acquiring citizenship in Ghana
Examine the responsibilities of a Ghanaian citizen
Discuss good working attitudes
Dramatise the various ways citizens contribute to the development of the country

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge of human resource development in Ghana

indicators.description: Mention ways of developing human resource in Ghana

exemplars.description: Explain the concepts: Human resource and Human resource development
Identify ways of developing human resource in Ghana
Discuss the importance of human resource development in Ghana
Assess the challenges associated with human resource development in Ghana
Suggest solutions to problems facing human resource development in Ghana

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of social security and pension issues

indicators.description: Examine the importance of social security to the individual

exemplars.description: Explain the concept of social security
Discuss the features of social security
Identify types of social security schemes
Think-pair-share the benefits of social security to the individual
Create a poster on the benefits of social security

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate knowledge on how tourism and leisure promote national development

indicators.description: Examine the role of tourism and leisure in socio-economic development of Ghana

exemplars.description: Explain the concepts: Tourism and Leisure
Identify some attractive places or sceneries in your locality
Examine reasons for which people go on tour to different places
Discuss the economic and social importance of tourism to the nation's development
Explain challenges faced in the tourism industry
Suggest ways of solving the challenges faced in the tourism industry
Discuss ways of promoting tourism in Ghana

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of how Ghana became an independent nation

indicators.description: Explain how events after the 1948 riots accelerated the move towards independence

exemplars.description: Show documentaries or listen to personal accounts on the 28th February riots
Discuss the documentaries or what was witnessed on the visit
Discuss the reasons for the formation of the Watson commission
Examine how the Watson Commission helped the move towards independence
Write down the bio data of the three ex-service men

indicators.description: Recount the formation of the Convention People's Party (CPP) in 1949

exemplars.description: Show and discuss pictures of Kwame Nkrumah, Kojo Botsio and K.A. Gbedemah
Discuss the role of other groups in the activities of the CPP
Use resource persons to tell about 'Positive Action'
Create a poster on one of the CPP leaders

indicators.description: Discuss the recommendations of the Coussey Committee and the outcomes of the 1951, 1954 and 1956 elections

exemplars.description: Discuss how the Coussey Committee recommendations formed the basis of the 1950 Constitution
Discuss the outcome of the 1951 elections
Discuss the role of Kwame Nkrumah as leader of government business
Examine why a new constitution was drawn up in 1954
Discuss what happened after the CPP won the 1956 election

indicators.description: Analyse the nature of government from 1957 to 1960

exemplars.description: Discuss the power-sharing arrangement between the British government and elected Ghanaian officials
Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of power-sharing from March 1957 to July 1960
Find out the portfolios held by British and Ghanaian officials
Discuss the composition of the cabinet from March 1957 to July 1960
